::: {#thm-append-length}
#### Appending adds lengths

For all lists $L$ and $M$ (@def-list),

$$
\operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}(L, M)} = \operatorname{len}(L) + \operatorname{len}(M),
$$

where $\operatorname{len}$ is the length (@def-list-length) and $\operatorname{app}$ is the append (@def-append).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $M$ be a list.
We use structural induction (@def-structural-induction) on $L$,
with $P(L)$ the equation $\operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}(L, M)} = \operatorname{len}(L) + \operatorname{len}(M)$.

**Base case.**
The base case of @def-list names only the empty list, and

$$
\ba
\operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}(\mathtt{empty}, M)}
&= \operatorname{len}(M)
&& \text{(definition of } \operatorname{app} \text{)}
\\&= 0 + \operatorname{len}(M)
\\&= \operatorname{len}(\mathtt{empty}) + \operatorname{len}(M).
&& \text{(definition of } \operatorname{len} \text{)}
\ea
$$

**Inductive step.**
The recursive rule builds $\operatorname{cons}(x, L)$ from an element $x$ and a list $L$.
Suppose $P(L)$.
Then

$$
\ba
& \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}\paren{\operatorname{cons}(x, L), M}}
\\&= \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{cons}\paren{x, \operatorname{app}(L, M)}}
&& \text{(definition of } \operatorname{app} \text{)}
\\&= 1 + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}(L, M)}
&& \text{(definition of } \operatorname{len} \text{)}
\\&= 1 + \operatorname{len}(L) + \operatorname{len}(M)
&& \text{(induction hypothesis } P(L) \text{)}
\\&= \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{cons}(x, L)} + \operatorname{len}(M),
&& \text{(definition of } \operatorname{len} \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is $P\paren{\operatorname{cons}(x, L)}$.
By structural induction, $P(L)$ holds for every list $L$.
Since $M$ was any list, the equation holds for all lists $L$ and $M$.

:::

:::
